---
title: "datashield-workflows"
subtitle: "Reusable GitHub Actions workflows for R packages and DataSHIELD analysis projects"
---

This repository holds **reusable workflows** (`on: workflow_call`) for R
package repositories: checks, releases, and bot suggestions for
documentation, tests and contributor credits. For DataSHIELD **analysis
projects**, a workflow drafts tested starter scripts from an analysis
plan. Each repository only needs thin *caller* files that point here, so
CI logic is written once instead of being copied into every repository.

A caller is a normal workflow file in your repository whose job `uses:` a
workflow from here:

```yaml
jobs:
  check:
    uses: nfdi4health/datashield-workflows/.github/workflows/r-cmd-check.yml@main
```

::: {.callout-note}
## Work in progress
The examples reference `@main`, which gets every change first. Version 1
is being prepared as the first release to pin to (`@v1`); see
[what changes for callers](roadmap.qmd#recent-changes). Feedback on what
you need is very welcome, see [Roadmap and open questions](roadmap.qmd).
:::

## Workflows

| Group | Workflow | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| Pull request checks | [R CMD check](r-cmd-check.qmd) | `R CMD check` on an OS × R version matrix, optional Codecov upload |
| | [Commitlint](commitlint.qmd) | Checks that commit messages follow Conventional Commits |
| | [Require head branch](require-head-branch.qmd) | Only lets PRs into a branch (e.g. `main`) come from one branch (e.g. `dev`) |
| Release | [Release chain](release.qmd) | How the release workflows below fit together |
| | [Package release](package-release.qmd) | Versions, tags and drafts a GitHub release with semantic-release |
| | [Merge pull request](merge-pull-request.qmd) | Merges a PR from a workflow |
| | [Create issue](create-issue.qmd) | Opens an issue when a check fails |
| | [Trigger release publish](trigger-release-publish.qmd) | Starts the release as a separate run |
| Bot suggestions | [How suggestions work](suggestions.qmd) | Shared mechanics: suggestion PRs, scheduled runs and full reviews, settings |
| | [Choosing suggestions](suggestion-choices.qmd) | Keep or decline single suggestions of a bot PR by checkbox |
| | [Author suggestions](authors-suggest.qmd) | Credits the contributors of a pull request in `DESCRIPTION` |
| | [Roxygen suggestions](roxygen-suggest.qmd) | Claude reviews and rewrites roxygen2 documentation |
| | [Test suggestions](test-suggest.qmd) | Claude reviews and writes testthat tests; only passing ones are proposed |
| | [Claude setup](claude-setup.qmd) | Keyless Claude API access for the two workflows above and the analysis scripts |
| | [Cleanup suggestion branch](cleanup-suggestion-branch.qmd) | Deletes bot branches once their PR is closed |
| | [Under the hood](suggestions-internals.qmd) | How the roxygen and test suggestions work, step by step |
| Analysis projects | [DataSHIELD analysis scripts](datashield-analysis-suggest.qmd) | Drafts starter scripts from your analysis plan, tested on mock data in DSLite |
| DataSHIELD naming (draft) | [Naming check and apply](ds-naming.qmd) | Checks packages against shared [naming rules](ds-naming-rules.qmd) and renames what people approve |
| Issue flow | [Issue label check](issue-label-check.qmd) | Removes the approval label if the wrong person set it or the issue changed afterwards |
| | [Issue triage](issue-triage.qmd) | A first look at new issues: one category, a short reason and a label |
| Workflow upkeep | [Workflow keepalive](workflow-keepalive.qmd) | Keeps scheduled workflows from being disabled after 60 days of inactivity |
| | [Workflow graphs](workflow-graphs.qmd) | Writes an overview of your workflows — table and diagrams — into `.github/workflow-graphs/README.md` |

## Where to start

1. [Getting started](getting-started.qmd) — branch model, secrets and the
   GitHub App most workflows rely on.
2. [How it fits together](overview.qmd) — diagrams of what runs when.
3. [Branch protection](branch-protection.qmd) — the rules the workflows
   are designed around.
4. Copy the example caller of each workflow you want into
   `.github/workflows/` of your repository.

Open questions and planned work are listed under
[Roadmap and open questions](roadmap.qmd).
